original_question: In astrophysics, determine the dynamical origin of quasars and pulsars, explain why gravitons have not been observed if gravity is mediated by a particle, decide whether the precession of planets other than Mercury can be predicted and matched with data, and determine whether traversable stargates or Einstein-Rosen bridges are physically possible and what conditions would keep such a bridge open without violating causality.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2.1-3.2.4 of the paper, under "3.2 Some open problems in Astrophysics": the four adjacent open questions titled "Quasar & Pulsars," "Graviton," "Precession of planets other than Mercury," and "Stargate."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper and preserves almost all of its substance: it tracks the four consecutive open questions in Section 3.2 on (i) the dynamical origin of quasars and pulsars, (ii) the non-observation of the graviton, (iii) precession of planets other than Mercury and comparison with observation, and (iv) the physical possibility of a stargate/Einstein-Rosen bridge together with causality-preserving conditions for keeping it open.
missing_details: The paper does not pose one unified problem here; it poses four separate but adjacent open questions in Section 3.2.1-3.2.4, so a paper-faithful rewrite should signal that this is a compound question rather than a single theorem-like statement.

For the quasar/pulsar item, the paper adds the specific hypothesis: "Are they ejected from the centres of galaxy(es)?" Your draft keeps the general origin question but omits this more exact subquestion.
For the stargate item, the paper makes the question conditional: "Provided general relativity is correct". That assumption should be retained.

The paper's stargate question is phrased as the possibility of creating a "real stargate" ("some theoreticians call it Einstein-Rosen Bridge") enabling travel "from one place in this galaxy to another galaxy"; your draft keeps the bridge idea but omits this exact travel scenario.

The paper further asks what conditions would keep the stargate open while "connecting the same places, so people could travel back to where they came from" without violating the causality principle; the return-trip/same-places condition is implicit in your draft and should be made explicit.

For the planetary-precession item, the paper first asks "Why didn't general relativity predict precession of planets other than Mercury?" and only then asks whether these effects can be predicted and compared with observation. That explanatory first clause should be retained verbatim or near-verbatim.

No mathematical notation, ambient ring/field, variables, operator definitions, homogeneity assumptions, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, or asymptotic quantifiers such as "for all sufficiently large m" occur in this target passage; adding any such structure would not be paper-faithful.
refined_question: In Section 3.2.1-3.2.4, the paper asks the following compound astrophysical/relativistic question: What is the dynamical origin of quasars and pulsars, and are they ejected from the centres of galaxies; why has the graviton not been observed experimentally, supposing it is the particle carrying the gravitational field; why did general relativity not predict the precession of planets other than Mercury, and can those precession effects be predicted and compared with observation; and, provided general relativity is correct, is it possible to create a real stargate (sometimes called an Einstein-Rosen bridge) enabling travel from one place in this galaxy to another galaxy, and if so, under what conditions could it be kept open while continuing to connect the same places so that return travel is possible without violating the causality principle?
justification: The draft is not aiming at a mathematical conjecture such as a Conjecture 1.1/Proposition 1.2/Theorem 1.3 framework; rather, it is essentially a near-paraphrase of four consecutive open questions in the paper's astrophysics section. The wording of the draft matches the sequence and content of Section 3.2.1-3.2.4 closely enough that the most faithful refinement is to preserve those four questions, restore the paper's dropped conditions and subclauses, and avoid introducing any extra formalism or broader neighboring problems. The nearby context supplies only sectional framing ("Some open problems in Astrophysics") and no additional notation or equivalence claims, so no alternate theorem-style reformulation is justified.
